Rules, guided-creator, migration, and browser test suites have not been run for this family yet.

Allies, Contacts, and Mentor remain deliberately unresolved for Alchemical's Backgrounds catalog: Exalted: The Autochthonians never mentions these three shared ids in either direction, unlike Lunar's own Background section, which explicitly confirms its unaltered shared ids remain available. notes: Exalted: The Autochthonians supplied and inventory complete cover-to-cover. 207 rows reviewed and inventoried under docs/references/exalted1e/alchemical/inventory/: the Chapter Two character-creation overview (plus bonus-point/experience-cost tables), the universal Anima Effect/Anima Banner table, the Alchemical Physiology section (Artificial Metabolism, Life and Death, Refitting/Essence Advancement/Evolution), all five Castes (Orichalcum, Moonsilver, Jade, Starmetal, Soulsteel) plus the apocryphal Adamant Caste sidebar, the full Clarity Trait (gain/loss/effects table) and its Dissonance/Gremlin Syndrome mirror, the new/altered Backgrounds (Class, Vats, Artifact, Backing, Familiar, Manse) plus the Building Vats in Creation sidebar and the Followers/Influence/Resources exclusion note, all of Chapter Three (pp. 87-141/PDF 88-142, 94 Charms across all nine Charm trees plus the two General Charms and the Charm-system framing), the full Chapter Four weaving-protocol catalog (49 rows, printed pp. 142-159/PDF 143-160), the rest of Chapter Four's character-facing material (31 rows: the three Autochthonian-only alchemy formulae, the full Autochthonian Technology artifact catalog, and the full Warfare and Transportation sections, completing all of Chapter Four), and the adventure-seed Chapters Five through Seven (reviewed and confirmed almost entirely GM/NPC/plot content, contributing exactly one more player-facing item, the Steamcar Refurbished vehicle). Chapter Four's Storyteller-side lore/NPC/setting material and Chapters Five-Seven's adventure narrative were reviewed and intentionally excluded as out of character-creation scope. No Alchemical-specific Merits/Flaws were found beyond Gremlin Syndrome/Dissonance anywhere in the book itself. A second source book, the Exalted Players Guide, closes the universal Merits & Flaws gap: 70 more rows (35 merits + 35 flaws) were derived from Lunar's already-verified transcription of that book's universal Chapter One (88 pg- rows total across all five planned families), evaluating each row's own splat-eligibility notes against Alchemical's core-book rules; 18 of the 88 were skipped as inapplicable to a soulless, vat-built construct Exalt (explicit other-splat-only restrictions, or ruled out by lacking blood lineage/reincarnation/Sorcery access/a childhood phase/being already permanently sterile). Several included rows were adapted for Alchemical's construct nature (chassis damage instead of flesh scarring, Class instead of Resources, a benefactor instead of parents, Clarity instead of the Great Curse, and a note that Sun-Seared and Hidden Manse are only fully relevant once a story reaches Creation), each flagged in that row's own notes. Two more small universal artifact catalogs were added afterward: six rows (Ghost Cestus, Sling Bow of Ice, The Golden Viper, Land Ship, Singing Staff, Eye of Autochthon) derived unchanged from Lunar's already-verified transcription of the Exalted Storyteller's Companion's universal Chapter Four 'Further Wonders' catalog, transferring cleanly except for two flagged judgment calls (The Golden Viper's flesh-to-gold bite is ambiguous for a vat-built frame; the Eye of Autochthon's Creation-native powers, despite its thematic tie to Autochthon himself, are only meaningful once a story reaches Creation); and eight rows freshly transcribed from Savage Seas' 'Artifacts of the Waves' naval catalog (Cargo Preservation Spindles, Armor of Aquatic Puissance, Steelsilk Sails, Storm Sapphire, Cord of Winds, Wavecleaver Daiklaive, Light Implosion Bow, Lightning Ballista), each kept selectable but flagged with an Autochthonia-has-no-Creation-style-oceans caveat mirroring the Sun-Seared/Hidden Manse precedent. 291 total rows now inventoried; nothing promoted to a production catalog yet. Locked pending schema/rules/creator/editor implementation and passing tests across all five planned families. A final cross-splat supplement-triage pass added 14 rows (291 -> 305) from Exalted: Blood and Salt: a Lintha-connection Character Backgrounds reinterpretation sidebar, a Bluehaven approach-navigation rule, four regional Character Concepts lists, seven new Artifacts (including the Talisman of the Cult of Dukantha, which grants Infernal sorcery access), one new Hearthstone (Jewel of Stability), three mundane equipment items; the rest of the book's NPC/monster stat-block material was reviewed and confirmed out of scope, and four reprinted artifacts (plus, where applicable, a reprinted Hearthstone and two reprinted/superseded spells) received citation notes on their existing rows rather than new duplicate rows. promotableEntries (207) is a preliminary keyword-based estimate of rows meant to become a strict catalog entry (Charms/Submodules, Merits/Flaws including Alchemical-only Dissonance variants, Backgrounds -- no Sorcery, per this splat's no-Sorcery design), matching Abyssal's approach in verification.ts. This has not been verified against a real built catalog and should be treated as approximate until Alchemical's own schema/catalog phase recomputes it precisely. Phase 1a (schema wiring plus Backgrounds and Merits/Flaws catalog promotion) added `'alchemical'` to `exaltedSheetTypes` in definitions.ts, making it a legal, schema-validated stored `sheetType` for the first time, without adding it to `definition.tsx`'s `variants` -- it remains unreachable through the character-creation UI, exactly like Lunar, Abyssal, and Sidereal before their own later UI phases. `promotedEntries` (77) breaks down as 6 Backgrounds ids (`alchemicalBackgrounds` in definitions.ts: the two wholly new ids Class and Vats from Exalted: The Autochthonians Chapter Two's 'Expanded Backgrounds,' plus the four altered shared ids Artifact, Backing, Familiar, and Manse, each carrying Alchemical-specific mechanics per that same section) plus 71 Merits/Flaws entries in the shared `dragonblooded-merits-flaws.json` catalog now carrying `'alchemical'` in `appliesTo` (`alchemicalOnlyTraits`). Those 71 catalog entries resolve the 70 `pg-merit-*`/`pg-flaw-*` inventory rows one-for-one, except the single inventoried 'Favor' row, which maps onto the catalog's existing `favor-merit`/`favor-flaw` split pair (hence 70 rows -> 71 catalog entries); no wholly new Alchemical-only catalog entries were needed, since every row the inventory's own judgment-call notes adapted (chassis damage instead of flesh scarring, Class instead of Resources, a benefactor instead of parents, etc.) kept its underlying mechanic and point cost unchanged, reframing flavor text only. Cross-checked the Destiny Merit specifically, since Abyssal/Sidereal both needed a `sharedCostOverrides` entry for it: the Players Guide's own 'Destiny and Exaltation' sidebar names Alchemical Exalted (alongside Dragon-Blooded) as explicitly uncapped, so Alchemical correctly falls through to the shared Dragon-Blooded-derived 1-5 point range with no override entry required, unlike Abyssal's and Sidereal's narrower 1-2 point cap. Deliberately excluded three shared Background ids -- Allies, Contacts, and Mentor -- from `alchemicalBackgrounds` despite their silent availability in Lunar's own equivalent list: Exalted: The Autochthonians' 'Expanded Backgrounds' section is an exhaustive catalog of every departure from the default framework (two additions, four alterations, one explicit three-Background exclusion folding Followers/Influence/Resources into Class), and never mentions these three ids in either direction, unlike Lunar's own text, which affirmatively confirms its unaltered shared ids remain available. Rather than guess, this project's 'never fabricate mechanics not confirmed in inventoried source text' rule holds these three back as an explicitly tracked open blocker pending a source that actually settles the question. Alchemical's Charms (94 rows), Weaving Protocols (49 rows), Alchemy Formulae, and the Clarity/submodule-installation Charm-slot subsystem remain completely out of scope for this phase -- `charmIdsBySheetType` in schema.ts still carries only a placeholder empty `Set()` for `alchemical`, so a blank Alchemical character validates with zero Charm/Combo/spell selections but any non-empty selection is correctly rejected as unknown, exactly matching how Lunar's own Charms were unimplemented before its later Phase 1b. Phase 1b (Charms catalog promotion) added `src/games/exalted1e/reference/alchemical-charms.json` and an `alchemical-powers.ts` reference module (mirroring lunar-powers.ts), promoting all 96 of the 94 named-tree Charms plus the 2 universal General Charms found in Chapter Three (pp. 89-141/PDF 90-142) to a production catalog, validated by a Zod schema and a 96-length superRefine uniqueness/prerequisite-integrity check. The 5 'framing' rows under the same Chapter Three heading pattern that describe systems rather than purchasable Charms (Charm Slots/Panoplies/Submodules/Arrays, Designing New Charms, Limitations and Effect, Alchemical Martial Artists, Identifying Charms) were deliberately excluded, matching this project's governance rule against promoting reference-only/calculated rows into a selectable catalog. Unlike every other already-promoted splat, Alchemical Charms are each keyed to a governing Attribute rather than an Ability (confirmed directly from the source's own Charm Slot rules: 'Dedicated' Charm Slots -- the ones that grant a Caste/Favored discount -- only accept Charms tied to a Favored or Caste Attribute, never an Ability), so `minimumRequirements` names the Attribute directly (e.g. `{ trait: 'Dexterity', rating: 3 }`) and `ability` stays `null` throughout, exactly like Lunar's own nullable `ability` field; `charmCategory` records the Charm's tree (General, Close Combat 15, Ranged Combat 11, Might and Mobility 14, Social 12, Stealth and Disguise 9, Sensory and Spiritual 10, Medical 11, Cognitive 9, Essence and Weaving 3, summing to exactly 96). The sole exception, Perfected Lotus Matrix, is explicitly keyed to the Martial Arts Ability instead (its own text states this is exactly why it can never be Favored/Caste for any Alchemical and must occupy a General Slot), captured without any schema change by simply naming 'Martial Arts' as the `minimumRequirements` trait. Two Charms (`transitory-augmentation-of-attribute`, `sustained-augmentation-of-attribute`) are each really nine separately-purchased/installed Charms, one per Attribute, and one (`material-synthesis-wave-emitter`) is really six Charms in one family (five Magical Materials plus adamant); all three are kept as single templated catalog rows with a literal `'(Attribute)'`/generic trait name, matching how the source itself presents them, rather than fabricating near-duplicate rows the source never actually tabulates separately. `prerequisiteCharms` resolves every cleanly-identifiable named prerequisite to a real catalog id (including compound 'Transitory or Sustained Augmentation of X' and 'Both Transitory and Sustained Augmentation of X' phrasing, which both resolve to the same underlying id pair since this project's `CharmComboRules`-adjacent prerequisite-id list is informational/cross-reference metadata, not an AND/OR-enforcing rules engine -- the original AND/OR nuance is preserved verbatim in `prerequisiteText` for any human reading the sheet). Alchemicals do not build ad hoc Combos the way other splats do; instead, per the Charm Slots/Panoplies/Submodules/Arrays framing row (pp. 89-90), any Attribute-based Charm may be bundled with others into a permanently surgically-installed 'Array' at a reduced combined installation cost, granting automatic access to every legal Combo among its members. `comboRules.eligible` therefore represents Array-eligibility (this family's real Combo-analog) rather than ordinary ad hoc Combo-eligibility, defaulting to `true` for every Charm except the four explicitly barred by their own text or by the framing row's blanket exclusion of supernatural martial arts Charms from Arrays (Perfected Lotus Matrix, Auxiliary Essence Storage Unit, Man-Machine Weaving Engine, God-Machine Weaving Engine); the Array mechanic itself (reduced-cost calculation, unit install/remove) is a distinct subsystem deferred to a future phase, exactly like Lunar's own deferred Great Curse/Shapechanging-Forms subsystem. The two Essence and Weaving 'engine' Charms (Man-Machine/God-Machine Weaving Engine) are promoted here as the gateway Charms into the Weaving Protocol subsystem, each explicitly cross-referenced in its own description to the still-out-of-scope pp. 145-159 catalog; installing either permanently grants 1 dot of Clarity and neither can ever be removed, both captured verbatim in each Charm's `description` text rather than a new schema field, since this phase does not yet model Clarity mechanically. `charmIdsBySheetType.alchemical` in schema.ts now resolves to the real 96-entry `alchemicalCharmIds` set (was an empty placeholder); Sorcery spells remain correctly rejected since Alchemical has no Sorcery access by design (Weaving Protocol is its own distinct, still-unpromoted system). `promotedEntries` grew from 77 to 173 (77 Phase 1a Backgrounds/Merits-Flaws + 96 Phase 1b Charms); `checksum` was populated for the first time with the real value computed by `scripts/audit-exalted-sources.mjs` (9006867c), since `alchemical-charms.json` is the first `alchemical-`-prefixed catalog file this family has ever had (Phase 1a's Backgrounds/Merits-Flaws promotions live in `definitions.ts`/the shared `dragonblooded-merits-flaws.json`, outside the audit script's glob, exactly as Sidereal's and Abyssal's own precedent already established). Full verification battery run: typecheck, lint, format check, the full unit test suite (all passing, including the new 14-test `alchemical-charms-catalog.test.ts` and the extended Charm-selection coverage in `exalted1e-alchemical.test.ts`), `scripts/audit-exalted-sources.mjs` (0 issues), the Exalted e2e smoke specs, and a production build. Exalted1eEditor.tsx remains untouched this phase, exactly as Phase 1a left it -- Alchemical stays fully locked out of definition.tsx's user-facing variants list and unreachable through the character-creation UI. Phase 1c (Weaving Protocol/Alchemy Formulae promotion) added `src/games/exalted1e/reference/alchemical-weaving-protocols.json` (38 rows) and `alchemical-formulae.json` (3 rows), both validated through new Zod schemas and exports added to the existing `alchemical-powers.ts` module rather than new standalone files, mirroring `lunar-powers.ts`'s own single-module convention. Of the 49 total Chapter Four Weaving Protocol rows (printed pp. 142-159/PDF 143-160), only the 38 `disposition: 'selectable'` rows were promoted: excluded are 5 reference-only framing rows describing the subsystem itself (`alchemical-protocols-overview`, `what-works-where-sidebar`, `man-machine-protocols-framing`, `spells-that-crossed-over-sidebar`, `god-machine-protocols-framing`) and 6 `gm-only` full NPC/creature stat blocks for the elemental Golems/automata summoned exclusively by the single selectable protocol `the-makers-instantaneous-forge` (`engine-golem-steam-automaton`, `glass-golem-crystal-automaton`, `magnet-golem-lightning-automaton`, `oil-golem-oil-automaton`, `smudge-golem-smoke-automaton`, `steel-golem-metal-automaton`) -- both exclusions matching this project's established convention against promoting framing/sidebar text or GM-only creature stat blocks into a player-facing selectable catalog. Unlike every other already-promoted splat's spell system, Weaving Protocols are gated by a fixed Minimum Clarity rating (parsed directly from each row's own 'Minimum Clarity N' sentence into a new `minimumClarity` field) rather than Essence + an Ability, with one row (`incarnation-of-bestial-malice`) also carrying a Maximum Clarity 7 cap captured in a parallel `maximumClarity` field, and `transcendent-pattern-weaving-protocol` requiring Minimum Clarity 10, the highest gate in the catalog (and the one protocol confirmed to work only in the Wyld). Any extra non-Clarity requirement text (e.g. `vat-surrogate-reweaving-technique`'s Vats-Background-with-Charms-on-retainer requirement, `soul-archiving-protocol`'s Backing 4+ requirement, `essence-matrix-inversion-procedure`'s one-day-advance-preparation requirement) is preserved verbatim in a new `requirementsText` field rather than discarded. A new `echelon` field ('man-machine'/'god-machine') records which of the two Weaving Engine Charms (promoted in Phase 1b) is needed, splitting 23 Man-Machine and 15 God-Machine Protocols, matching the inventory's own Chapter Four structure. Because every Weaving Protocol has the same fixed-cost/fixed-gate/discrete-effect shape as an ordinary Sorcery spell (unlike Sidereal's fully freeform Astrology Resplendent Effects, which stay an unautomated `sidereal-astrology.ts` reference panel), Weaving Protocols are validated as real, schema-checked selections through the same `powers.spells` bucket Sorcery/Necromancy spells already use, via a new `alchemicalWeavingProtocolIds` Set checked in `schema.ts` -- replacing the prior shared Alchemical/Fair-Folk placeholder branch (which incorrectly claimed Alchemical 'has no Sorcery/spell system at all... expected to remain permanent') with a real Alchemical-specific branch, while leaving Fair Folk's own placeholder branch intact and correctly labeled. Several protocols explicitly defer their full cost/target/duration to a named Sorcery spell rather than restating it ('identical to', 'equivalent to', or 'the same as' the named spell); cross-checked every such name against the shared `dragonblooded-sorcery.json` catalog and captured the match in a new `equivalentSorcerySpellId` field (asserted at module load time to resolve to a real shared-catalog id, exactly like `lunarSorcerySpellIds`'s own load-time assertion): `crystal-lotus-of-repose` (Sleep of Stony Safety), `lightning-elemental-concatenation-protocol` (Lightning Spider), `sonic-hammer-vocalization` (Thunder Wolf's Howl), `summon-autochthonian-elemental` (Summon Elemental), `vision-transmitting-protocol` (Infallible Messenger), `machine-soul-essence-baffle` (Mercury's Deliverance), `pattern-suspension-protocol` (Eternal Crystalline Encasement), and `plague-of-bronze-snakes` (Plague of Bronze Snakes -- same name, same Savant and Sorcerer p. 112 citation as the shared catalog's existing entry, a genuine confirmed match rather than an id collision, even though the Alchemical protocol row and the shared spell row happen to share the literal id string; the two stay fully independent catalog entries, each with its own id/name/summary, exactly as the source presents the protocol as its own purchasable thing that merely reuses an existing spell's effect). Left `null` for two further protocols that likewise name a specific spell they defer to (`maser-palm-technique` to 'Blood of Boiling Oil', `instantaneous-transfer-protocol` to 'Travel Without Distance') because neither spell exists in the shared catalog today -- both appear to be drawn from the Exalted core rulebook's own spell list, which `dragonblooded-sorcery.json` does not yet cover (it was built from Savant and Sorcerer/Book of Three Circles); rather than guess at an id or fabricate a new spell entry, these two keep their deferred-mechanics text in `description` only, flagged for a future phase if the core rulebook is ever inventoried. Also deliberately left `null` for `summon-machine-spirit` despite naming Summon Elemental, since its own text says it only 'functions like' that spell while summoning a genuinely different kind of being (a machine spirit, not an elemental) -- a narrative comparison, not a true mechanical defer like the 8 confirmed matches. The 3 Alchemy Formulae rows (`sweet-sleep-surrogate-syrup`, `friction-banishing-preparation`, `the-makers-inertial-bile`, printed p. 161/PDF 162) are each gated by an 'Alchemy' dot rating plus a Minimum Backing rating plus an Intelligence + Occult roll -- none of which this app's character schema models as a trait anywhere, and this app has no dice-rolling engine to automate the roll either way. Building a dedicated new trait field to validate purchase of just 3 rows would be overengineering relative to every other family's precedent, so `alchemicalFormulae` stays a small browsable reference catalog (Zod-validated for shape, but never wired into `powers.spells` or any other character-selection schema), matching `sidereal-astrology-rules.json`'s own precedent of counting toward `promotedEntries` via the audit script's `${family}-*.json` glob despite being unautomated reference text. `promotableEntries` is recomputed this phase from the prior 207 preliminary keyword-based estimate (flagged since Phase 1a as approximate) to a precise 214 (6 Backgrounds + 71 Merits/Flaws + 96 Charms + 38 Weaving Protocols + 3 Alchemy Formulae), now exactly matching `promotedEntries`, which rose from 173 to 214; `checksum` was recomputed to 1d839847 by `scripts/audit-exalted-sources.mjs` now that `alchemical-weaving-protocols.json` and `alchemical-formulae.json` have joined `alchemical-charms.json` under the family's own `alchemical-*.json` glob. Full verification battery re-run: typecheck, lint, format check, the full unit test suite (all passing, including the new 13-test `alchemical-weaving-protocols-catalog.test.ts` and the extended spell-selection coverage in `exalted1e-alchemical.test.ts`), `scripts/audit-exalted-sources.mjs` (0 issues), the Exalted e2e smoke specs, and a production build. Exalted1eEditor.tsx remains untouched this phase too -- Alchemical stays fully locked out of definition.tsx's user-facing variants list and unreachable through the character-creation UI; the Clarity Trait, Charm-Slot/Panoply/Array installation tracking, and any editor UI wiring for this family all remain out of scope, deferred to a future phase. Correction for this and the prior note: Exalted1eEditor.tsx was never actually gated on definition.tsx's variants list for an already-existing character record -- ExaltedFamilyStatePanel.tsx, a pre-existing shared component Exalted1eEditor.tsx renders unconditionally for every Exalted character regardless of sheetType, already had a full (if stale-catalog-referencing) Alchemical branch wired in before this phase, built against the unverified OCR draft in ./reference/family-powers rather than the real alchemical-powers.ts catalog and referencing a non-existent installationCost field. 'Unreachable through the character-creation UI' was and remains true only for creating a brand-new Alchemical record; it was never true for editing one that already exists (e.g. an imported or hand-authored record), a distinction prior phases' notes stated imprecisely. This phase (Clarity Trait plus Charm-Slot/Panoply/Array installation tracking) redesigns familyState's Alchemical shape from a single flat clarity: number (0-10) and a single charmSlots: number (0-99) into five fields: clarityPermanent (0-10, described in Exalted: The Autochthonians p. 69 as effectively irreversible, gained only from Essence above 5 or certain installed Charms) and clarityTemporary (0-10, fluctuating via Virtue-suppression gains and human-contact/embracing-Virtue losses -- session-level trigger events this app has no way to observe or automate), replacing the single ambiguous clarity number; and dedicatedSlots (0-99) and generalSlots (0-99), replacing the single charmSlots number, modeling the source's real distinction that Dedicated Slots only accept Charms tied to a Favored/Caste Attribute while General Slots accept any Charm (per the alchemical-charm-slots-panoplies-arrays inventory row). New schema-level invariants added to schema.ts's main superRefine: clarityPermanent + clarityTemporary must never exceed 10 (the Trait's real fixed maximum); clarityPermanent must be at least max(0, essence.rating - 5), the one Clarity rule precise enough to enforce as fixed arithmetic off an already-stored field (Inhuman Essence, p. 69) without simulating the unobservable Virtue/human-contact triggers; every installedCharmIds entry must resolve to a real id in alchemicalCharmIds and no id may repeat; and installedCharmIds.length may never exceed dedicatedSlots + generalSlots. Deliberately out of scope, matching this project's established anti-overengineering stance: enforcing the Dedicated-Slot Favored/Caste-Attribute restriction itself (would require cross-referencing creation.favoredAttributeIds/identity.caste against each Charm's governing Attribute, a creator-phase feature Alchemical does not have yet); Submodule reduced-installation-cost bookkeeping; and the Panoply (owned-but-uninstalled reserve Charms) concept, since this app has no separate Panoply-inventory UI anywhere. EXALTED1E_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped 11 -> 12 with a guarded migration step (skipped if clarityPermanent already exists on the record, so an already-migrated record is never silently clobbered back to defaults): legacy clarity maps to the new clarityTemporary, leaving clarityPermanent at a safe default of 0 (there is no way to know after the fact which part of an old flat number was meant to be the irreversible share, and fabricating a permanent value this app cannot un-fabricate later would violate the Inhuman Essence invariant's own spirit); legacy charmSlots maps to the new generalSlots, the more permissive of the two slot types, leaving dedicatedSlots at 0 (there is no way to verify after the fact whether an already-recorded installed Charm would have legally occupied a Dedicated Slot). profiles.ts's createDefaultFamilyState for 'alchemical' was updated to the new five-field shape; a blank character still starts all four numeric fields at 0 (not the canonical starting 4+4 Slots), matching this project's 'no false choices until a real creator phase exists' convention already used elsewhere (e.g. Sidereal's blank colleges: {}). Fixing the pre-existing ExaltedFamilyStatePanel.tsx Alchemical branch (required regardless, since the familyState field renames would otherwise have left it non-compiling) was done by extracting a new, catalog-accurate AlchemicalInstallationPanel.tsx component, following the same per-family sub-panel pattern already established by LunarShapechangingPanel.tsx and SiderealAstrologyPanel.tsx: two mutually-clamped DotRating controls for Permanent/Temporary Clarity (each passes max={10 - theOtherRating} so their sum can never visually or functionally exceed 10), Dedicated/General Slot number inputs (disabled outside build mode, matching how other irreversible-ish structural choices lock in Play; Clarity dots stay editable in Play mode since both its gain and loss are explicitly session-driven per the source text), a slot/mote usage summary, and an owned-Charms-only checkbox list (sourced from the real alchemicalCharmById map, not the stale OCR draft) that disables further installs once dedicatedSlots + generalSlots capacity is reached. Full verification battery run for this phase: a cache-busted clean tsc -b --force (discovered mid-phase that plain tsc --noEmit -p . was returning false-positive clean results against a stale node_modules/.tmp/*.tsbuildinfo cache after the familyState field renames; deleting the two cache files before re-running surfaced the real compile errors this phase then fixed), npm run lint (0 errors, only the same 10 pre-existing unrelated react-refresh/only-export-components warnings in untouched files), the full unit/integration suite (970 tests; 2 unrelated pre-existing test-runner timeouts in ars-magica-editor.test.tsx and mage20-module-editor.test.tsx, neither touched this phase, both confirmed passing in isolation -- a resource-contention artifact of running the full suite in parallel, not a regression), the full 87-spec Playwright e2e suite (all passing), scripts/audit-exalted-sources.mjs (0 issues; its own narrower promoted-row count rose 96 -> 137, the same already-established gap against this file's promotedEntries seen on every other certified-catalog-dimension family), and a production build. New coverage added: 9 new tests in exalted1e-alchemical.test.ts (7 for the Clarity-sum/Inhuman-Essence/installed-Charm-id invariants, 2 for the version-12 migration's real-legacy-data mapping and its already-migrated guard) plus a new 8-test tests/integration/alchemical-installation-panel.test.tsx exercising the extracted panel directly. Alchemical remains locked exactly as before: certifiedAt stays null, and Phase 6's all-five-families-together rule still prohibits adding Alchemical to definition.tsx's variants list on its own.
